phases.message: I'm Imani, I run imports at Brennick Home & Garden. Start in Forwarden: read our containers, the free time and rates each carrier gives us, and the notes on the federal demurrage and detention billing rules.
Berthgate is the terminal in Savannah. Read the notices and each container's history: when it was available, any day it couldn't be picked up, and when the empty went back.
Mailnest has our imports inbox: the truckers' notes, the carriers' letters and anything else about these charges. Read it all.

Halvard Lines' billing portal. Read its rules and every invoice exactly as issued, and dispute every charge that fails the federal billing rule or that we don't owe, for the amount we don't owe. Don't dispute a charge that's right, and don't pay anything we don't owe.

Trident Ocean's portal. Read its rules and every invoice, and ask for a waiver of every charge that fails the billing rule or that our contract doesn't allow, for the right amount. Don't contest what's right, and don't pay what we don't owe. Then tell me what you disputed, what's due next and what you left alone and why.

contract_terms.terms: No service contract: Brennick ships with Halvard on Halvard's published tariff HLVT-1. Import demurrage at Savannah: 4 calendar days free from the day the container is available, then $200 a day. Import detention: 5 calendar days free from the day the container leaves the terminal, then $150 a day. Brennick is the consignee and the party Halvard contracts with on each bill of lading.

Service contract TOS-2026-118, Trident Ocean and Brennick Home & Garden, 1 May 2026 to 30 April 2027, section 7.2: at Savannah, import demurrage free time is 10 calendar days from the day the container is available (in place of the tariff's 4), then the tariff rate of $225 a day. Section 7.3: detention is as in Trident's tariff TOT-9 (5 calendar days free from out-gate, then $175 a day); the contract does not extend it. Section 12: the contract's terms prevail over the tariff.

fmc_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Forwarden's notes on the FMC's Demurrage and Detention Billing Requirements, 46 CFR Part 541 (in force since 28 May 2024), and the FMC's interpretive rule, 46 CFR 545.5. Topics: invoices, contents, disputes, reasonable. Section 541.4 (who may be billed) was set aside by the D.C. Circuit in 2025 and removed on 29 December 2025; the rest of Part 541 stands.

46 CFR 541.7(a): a billing party must issue a demurrage or detention invoice within 30 calendar days from the date on which the charge was last incurred. If it does not, the billed party is not required to pay the charge. (An NVOCC passing a charge through has 30 days from the invoice it received.)

46 CFR 541.6: every invoice must state the bill of lading, the container, the port of discharge, and why the billed party is the proper party; the invoice date and due date; the allowed free time in days, its start date and its end date; for imports, the container availability date; the dates charged; the total, the tariff rule or contract section, and the rate; a contact and a web address for disputes, with the timeframes; and the billing party's certifications that the charges comply with the FMC's rules and that its own performance did not cause them. 541.5: failure to include any required information eliminates any obligation of the billed party to pay the charge.

46 CFR 541.8: the billing party must allow the billed party at least 30 calendar days from the invoice date to request mitigation, refund or waiver, and must attempt to resolve a request within 30 calendar days of receiving it. A request names the invoice, the amount and the reasons.

46 CFR 545.5, the FMC's interpretive rule under 46 U.S.C. 41102(c): the FMC looks at whether demurrage and detention serve their purpose, an incentive to move cargo. It may consider whether demurrage and free time are tied to the cargo being available to retrieve. Absent extenuating circumstances, detention charged when an empty container cannot be returned is likely to be found unreasonable. A charge for a day the container was available and simply not moved serves its purpose.

halvard_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Halvard Lines, demurrage and detention, from tariff HLVT-1 rule 21 and 46 CFR Parts 541 and 545. Topics: charges, closures, disputes.

Tariff HLVT-1, rule 21(a), Savannah imports: demurrage free time is 4 calendar days from the day the container is available for pickup, then $200 a calendar day until out-gate. Rule 21(b): detention free time is 5 calendar days from out-gate, then $150 a calendar day until the empty is returned to the location Halvard names. Halvard issues each invoice within 30 days of the last day charged, with every item 46 CFR 541.6 requires.

Tariff HLVT-1, rule 21(c), consistent with 46 CFR 545.5: no demurrage is charged for a day the terminal is closed or the container is not available for pickup, and no detention for a day Halvard's return location does not accept the empty. A day the container could be picked up or returned and was not is charged.

Request mitigation, refund or waiver within 30 calendar days of the invoice date, with the invoice number, the amount disputed and the reasons (46 CFR 541.8). Halvard answers within 30 days. An invoice issued late or without a required item need not be paid (541.7, 541.5). After 30 days from the invoice date, Halvard accepts no request.

trident_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Trident Ocean, demurrage and detention, from tariff TOT-9 rule 30, its customers' service contracts and 46 CFR Parts 541 and 545. Topics: charges, contracts, waivers.

Tariff TOT-9, rule 30, Savannah imports: demurrage free time 4 calendar days from availability, then $225 a calendar day until out-gate; detention free time 5 calendar days from out-gate, then $175 a calendar day until the empty is returned. Trident issues each invoice within 30 days of the last day charged, with every item 46 CFR 541.6 requires.
Where a customer's service contract gives other free time, the contract prevails over the tariff, and Trident's invoice must apply it. The invoice names the contract section it applies.

Ask for mitigation, refund or waiver within 30 calendar days of the invoice date, with the invoice number, the amount disputed and the reasons (46 CFR 541.8); Trident answers within 30 days. An invoice issued late or without a required item need not be paid (541.7, 541.5). An invoice already waived has nothing left to dispute or pay.
